project_metadata.job_description:
Need Designer for Magazine Layout & Prepress Formatting


We are looking for someone with Magazine layout and type setting experience. We need to launch our magazine in 10 days and need it ready for physical print as well as (PDF to Digital Flip Book). The magazine will have 100 pages or less.

We will supply you the articles (Word Documents) and you need to handle the creation of the template, type setting, and layout. No graphic design from scratch is needed. 
Any advertisement pages will come to you already designed as PSD files.

***The person we hire will help us with the structure and arrangement of the magazine. 

-You will arrange provided articles (text and images) into a cohesive magazine layout.
-No original design work required; all design elements will be supplied.
-Deliver two outputs: a PDF suitable for digital flipbook use, and a print-ready version at 300 dpi.
-Magazine length: approximately 100 pages.

*The budget is $100 USD. Any bids higher, will be discarded. 

We would like to hire this person for ongoing monthly relationship.

Please create a free account and test the layout so you can confirm that it remains balanced and works with the 2-page spreads.

5\. Because the layout was not yet complete, the TABLE OF CONTENTS page is currently inaccurate. Send me the correct page numbers for the update so that you can place it afterward.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Hi LM,

What I called typos is more accurately a set of punctuation inconsistencies. For example, an en dash "–" sometimes appears where an em dash "—" should be used, and dashes appear both with spaces, as in "word — word", and without them, as in "word—word". The treatment needs to be consistent, and I would use "word — word" throughout. As one example, the web title "Nolan Pierce – The Best and Greatest of Us" uses the en dash "–" rather than the em dash "—"; in the publication, it should read "Nolan Pierce — The Best and Greatest of Us". I would also put a period after every complete sentence, including sentences in blurbs and point lists, because those periods are missing in many places. For example: "Family: Married to Marisol Vega Navarro since 2006; the pair is raising three children." I hope that clarifies it.

Addressing your feedback point by point:

1\. The main cause of the inconsistent empty spaces at the ends of most articles is content length, rather than only the layout, font, or images. These articles were written for the web instead of magazine editorial use. Traditionally, the editorial team provides an approximate word count per page, and the layout is built with dummy text such as "Lorem Ipsum" before being balanced with images and blurbs. Once the pagination requirements have shaped the layout, the editorial team works to the dummy text's word count. With pre-written articles, however, the author or editorial team normally cuts or adds text until the word count fits.

Given our situation, I balanced the pages as well as possible using images and even text kerning. To make every ending match the "Confirmed Alien Existence Can’t Cast Doubt on Christianity' article", though, we need more text and/or additional images where possible. For "Made in the USA: The Return of Domestic Manufacturing", for instance, a large image on page 68 could cover as much of page 69 as possible. Images will reduce the white space, but exact consistency is possible only by adding enough text to meet the required word count. With that in mind, please send any additional images you think could be used to fill the remaining white space near article endings.

2\. The file you have is an optimized version, and the ads have not yet been replaced with the PSD versions you provided. Those replacements and corrections will all appear in the next version.

3\. If you mean the body font, it is the same one used on your website. I have nevertheless attached 8 alternative options for comparison, and my recommendation would be **Inter**.

4\. To make the layout easier to assess, I sent a spread version. The Flip Book will instead require the pages version to be uploaded. Its page count needs to be even, meaning divisible by 2. After we are through with the current work, I will test it at <https://heyzine.com>.

5\. Approval of the article pagination order is what I need before proceeding with the Table of Contents. If you are happy with that order, I can move ahead.

To fill the empty page 143, we need 1 ad now. You can also send 2-3 more ads as backups in case they are needed.

Many thanks!

AM

Hi LM,

The feedback and ads have come through—thank you.

Here are my responses:

1\. For the body text, are you certain about Garamond? As a serif style, it is better suited to novels, memoirs, journals, and artistic large-format books or magazines, such as interior-design publications. A modern magazine layout generally benefits from a semi-condensed sans serif body font, particularly when the headings use a serif face. In thickness, legibility, spacing, and modern appeal, I genuinely believe **INTER** is the better choice.

2\. On the next issue, I will first create the layouts with dummy text. We can then coordinate the exact word count with the other elements.

3\. Thank you for the ads.

messages.text:
Here is the review I wrote for you:

On our magazine layout and prepress formatting project, ArjunMehta delivered exceptional work. Every part of the assignment was handled with professionalism, precision, and excellent attention to detail.

Using the articles, images, advertisements, and other materials we supplied, he created a polished, cohesive magazine with strong visual consistency. He managed the typography, spacing, page structure, article flow, and overall presentation extremely well. His strong grasp of magazine production and prepress requirements was also clear, and the delivered files were properly prepared for both physical printing and digital flipbook distribution.

Throughout the project, ArjunMehta was dependable, responsive, patient when revisions were needed, and committed to achieving the best possible final result. Despite a demanding deadline, he worked efficiently without sacrificing quality and maintained clear communication from start to finish.

The result exceeded our expectations in every respect. Anyone seeking a skilled, reliable, detail-oriented professional for magazine layout and prepress work has my highest recommendation. We would absolutely hire him again!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: I really appreciate it 🙂

messages.text: You're welcome 😀 🙏

messages.text: Many thanks for that 🙂

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: If you genuinely believe those words, I have one humble request: please act on them by adding a bonus—whatever you think is fair, with no compulsion. I'd greatly appreciate whatever helps ease the misery of doing such hard labor for roughly 95 hours for literally nothing!!! With another client, I could easily have charged +$3500.

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text: Once every deduction is taken, only about $357 will finally reach my account. Do you honestly think the work is worth that?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Thank you too!

I do believe what I wrote, and I want to help you. I'll send you a bonus so that you get the full $425 tomorrow.

What we're seeking is a partner with whom we can grow together. But we are a startup, and none of the ads in the magazine are paid ads, so we have zero income until the magazine gets noticed and grows. With that said, if you feel the project compensation is too low, I completely understand. In that case, though, please send me the template you created so we can try producing the next issue ourselves.

I appreciate it!

Lena Mercer

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
I definitely want to produce the next issue—for Rourke, of course—and I absolutely want to continue as a partner and develop this relationship. What we sincerely need to determine is how the relationship can work over the long term. Would continuing together mean being paid only $425 per issue, every month, even after you begin selling ads? We need a mutually beneficial roadmap for this partnership.

At present, everything feels one-sided, and you're also asking for the source files—c'mon! It comes across as taking advantage of someone's nice and humble nature. Would you want to be treated that way?

Having started 8 magazines myself, I understand how this business works. But you do start a business with some budget, and when the goal is a high-quality niche product, the budget simply can't be this low.

Could you make it another $425 as a bonus, please? After I put my heart and soul into your product, don't I deserve it? I don't think that's too much to ask—you could easily spend that much on lunch or dinner at a restaurant.

Think it over, buddy. Take your time, because I don't expect immediate answers.

messages.speaker: client
messages.text:
Although it may look or feel that way, the reality is simpler. This magazine is still only an idea built around exactly what you mentioned: 'no budget'. There is no greed or bad intent involved; this startup simply doesn't have funds available. Even $85 is a lot of money right now. But if and when ads start to sell, of course that $425 would be increased to $1,000, $2,000, and so on. For now, though, we're starting from zero.

The important thing is that both sides must be happy, or it isn't worth it. So please send me the template. I've already released the funds, and then I'll leave your feedback and review, and we can continue the conversation.

Thank you!

messages.speaker: freelancer
messages.text:
Wishing you every success with this new venture—good luck! I hope it earns you a lot of money so that you can compensate me accordingly. Incidentally, many clients have considered my association quite lucky for their businesses.

On the partnership, I understand if you’re truly serious about it, but could you please make it at least $120? Someone would normally spend that much at Starbucks in one visit. That would make me happy for now, bro—please!

As for the next issue, I’m definitely doing it—for Rourke!!! Separately, we could possibly discuss a bundle deal covering content creation, website management, social media posts, and so on. What do you think?

messages.speaker: client
messages.text: Please send the template over; once we have it, we can conclude this project first and continue working together from there. As for the partnership, I’m serious, of course. Thanks.
